fieldMarks: Heavy-bodied rodent about 20–26 in long with a short (about 6 in) bristly tail; 5–15 lb.
Yellowish-brown to blackish-brown fur with sparse, paler belly hair; dark feet.
behavior: Active in early morning and late evening in summer.
Sharp alarm whistle; 'chuck-chuck' sounds while feeding.
Digs burrows with a main entrance marked by a dirt mound and inconspicuous back exits.
Hibernates from about October to early spring; eats grasses, clover, alfalfa, dandelion and crops.
habitat: Open fields, meadows, pastures, fencerows and woodland edges, preferring well-drained slopes.
range: From Oklahoma and Alabama north and northeast through the eastern US, and west across Canada into Alaska.
